quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

36 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: You must use low beams when:

options.text: Driving on a lit street.
Driving on a freeway.
Driving in fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving in fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams when driving in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off water droplets and create glare, making it harder to see. Some cars have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: When parking on a hill, you should:

options.text: Have one rear wheel touch the curb.
Use your parking brake and put the car in park.
Keep your front wheels parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and put the car in park.
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake and leave your car in park on a hill. If there is no curb, turn your front wheels so the car rolls away from traffic if brakes fail. If there is a curb, turn wheels toward it (going downhill) or gently away from it (going uphill).

questions.question: One solid yellow line and one broken yellow line mark the center of the road. If the broken line is next to your lane, it means:

options.text: You cannot pass in this area.
You can pass other vehicles on the left if no traffic is coming toward you.
You can only turn right in this area.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass other vehicles on the left if no traffic is coming toward you.
questions.explanation: When there is a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line, you can pass on the side next to the broken line.

questions.question: Which factor affects how fast a person absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: A person's weight, sex, the amount of food in their stomach, and how much they have drunk all affect alcohol absorption. Time is the only way to remove alcohol from the body.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You must drive through the intersection at the posted speed.
The highest safe speed is 55 mph.
You cannot drive slower than the posted speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest safe speed is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the maximum speed limit for that road. You can drive slower based on conditions, but you cannot drive faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Only in a crosswalk.
Always, even if they are not following traffic laws.
Only when the traffic light is in their favor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always, even if they are not following traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians near your car. Do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter the circumstances.

questions.question: After passing a car, it is safe to move back to your lane when:

options.text: The driver you passed signals for you to return.
You signal for three seconds.
You see the other car's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You see the other car's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror before moving back into your lane. When you see both headlights of the car you passed, you have enough room to return safely.

questions.question: On a slippery road, keep a following distance that is:

options.text: The same as normal.
Greater than normal.
Closer than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Greater than normal.
questions.explanation: You need more distance to stop on slippery roads. Increase your following distance when driving on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with no curb, turn your front wheels:

options.text: To the left (toward the street).
To the right (away from the street).
Straight with the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right (away from the street).
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels away from the street center on a hill with no curb. This way, your car rolls away from traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: Before passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not assume the other driver will make room for you to return.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you signal.
Assume the other driver will keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the other driver will make room for you to return.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will give you space or right-of-way, even if you signal.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, you should:

options.text: Be ready for a person or car to suddenly enter your lane.
Expect all drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
Drive close to the parked cars to leave room for other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or car to suddenly enter your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep space between your car and parked cars. Someone may step out suddenly or a driver may start moving without seeing you.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, drive at:

options.text: About the same speed as freeway traffic.
The legal speed limit.
Slower than freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: About the same speed as freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Enter the freeway at or near the speed of traffic, unless traffic is going faster than the legal speed limit.

questions.question: At night, an oncoming car has bright headlights on that are blinding you. You should:

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at bright headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the other car from the side of your eye.

questions.question: You should keep your signal on while turning because it:

options.text: Is illegal to turn off your signal before finishing a turn.
Tells other drivers what you plan to do.
Is always unsafe to turn off a signal before finishing a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This lets other drivers, riders, and pedestrians know your plans.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles are not allowed.
A bike shop is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to places where animals, people, and bicycles are likely to cross the road.

questions.question: A broken yellow line between two lanes means:

options.text: Both lanes go in the same direction.
Passing is allowed when it is safe.
Passing is not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A dashed yellow line separates lanes going opposite directions. You can pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: On a one-way street, you can turn left onto another one-way street only if:

options.text: You speed up before turning.
Traffic moves to the right.
Traffic moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You can turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves left, unless a sign says not to. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves right.

questions.question: An orange sign means:

options.text: There is construction ahead.
You must change lanes.
There is a detour ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is construction ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn of construction areas. Drive carefully through these areas.

questions.question: How do you know where traffic is behind you?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror often.
Turn and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror often to see traffic behind you.

questions.question: Your car can hydroplane on wet roads at speeds as low as:

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: At speeds up to 35 mph, tires can push water away. At speeds above 35 mph, tires lose grip and slide on water like water skis.

questions.question: After a train passes at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Wait for the signal lights to stop flashing.
Look for a second train.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Watch for a second train even after the first one passes. Do not move until the gates are fully raised and all warning lights stop flashing.

questions.question: You are in a turn lane ready to turn left, but there is oncoming traffic. You should:

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal before you reach the intersection.
Turn your front wheels to the left to prepare.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: Start signaling about 100 feet before the turn. Keep your front wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This protects you if another car hits you from behind.

questions.question: A broken yellow line in the center of a road means:

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means any driver can pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Which is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using high beam lights in fog.
Staring at the road ahead.
Checking your rearview mirrors often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your rearview mirrors often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors every 2 to 5 seconds to watch for hazards. Do not stare at just the road ahead. In fog, use low beam headlights, not high beams.

questions.question: Blue traffic signs give information about:

options.text: Motorist services.
Construction and maintenance.
Distance to specific locations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorist services.
questions.explanation: Blue signs show where to find motorist services like rest areas, food, or hospitals.

questions.question: Which statement is true about work zones?

options.text: Fines for violations in work zones are the same as normal traffic violations.
You must "Slow for the Cone Zone."
Slow down only if you see workers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must "Slow for the Cone Zone."
questions.explanation: Slow down through work zones. This keeps drivers, pedestrians, cyclists, and road workers safe.

questions.question: It is illegal to park your vehicle:

options.text: In an unmarked crosswalk.
Within three feet of a private driveway.
In a bicycle lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In an unmarked crosswalk.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a marked or unmarked crosswalk. You can park in a bicycle lane if there is no "No parking" sign and your car does not block bicyclists.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, it is safe to move back into the right lane when:

options.text: About three seconds have passed.
You can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
You can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can return to your lane when you see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always check your blind spots before moving.

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down:

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights.
Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Get your vehicle off the road and away from traffic. Turn on your hazard lights to warn other drivers.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings. This sign warns of a crosswalk. Be alert and let pedestrians cross safely.

questions.question: The speed limit is 65 mph, but traffic is heavy and moving at 35 mph. The best speed for your vehicle is:

options.text: 25 mph.
35 mph.
30 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 mph.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other traffic. Drive at the speed of traffic unless traffic exceeds the legal speed limit.

questions.question: Which roadways freeze first when wet?

options.text: Bridges and overpasses.
Intersections.
Tunnels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bridges and overpasses.
questions.explanation: Bridges and overpasses freeze before the rest of the road.

questions.question: Construction zone signs are generally:

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow.
Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols. They are placed on the right side of the road, or on both sides of a divided highway.

questions.question: You want to pass a cyclist in a narrow lane, but a car is coming. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn then pass the cyclist.
Slow down and let the car pass before passing the cyclist.
Wait until the cyclist leaves the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the car pass before passing the cyclist.
questions.explanation: Handle one danger at a time. Let the car pass first, then pass the cyclist safely.

questions.question: When passing a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Stay close in the same lane since the motorcycle is small.
Honk your horn so the motorcycle moves to the shoulder.
Stay completely in the left lane during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay completely in the left lane during the pass.
questions.explanation: Give the motorcycle a full lane. Never share the same lane. Returning to your lane too soon can force the rider off the road.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Missing an exit.
Being late for an appointment.
Falling asleep at the wheel and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep at the wheel and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue causes poor driving decisions and errors. You could fall asleep behind the wheel and crash, hurting yourself or others.
